answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 66% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned so that nobody profits from it. Because the tundra forfeiture is applied at exit, the ridge ledger totals each burn, and the grove audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 284 aliases therefore destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 36 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
